intro: You are now at the Mevlâna Museum, a museum in Konya province from the 13th century. Here lies the tomb of Mevlâna Celâleddin Rumi, with the Mevlevi lodge around it. Look up at the green-tiled dome: it is the emblem of Konya.
history: This building stands on ground that was once the rose garden of the Seljuk palace, given to Mevlâna's father. When Mevlâna died in 1273, a tomb was raised over him. Over the following centuries a semahane, dervish cells, kitchens and a fountain grew up around it, and together they became a Mevlevi lodge. In 1926 it opened as a museum.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Green Dome and the Semahane, then the Dervish cells, the Kitchen and the Manuscript collection.
facts: Did you know? The night Mevlâna died is called Şeb-i Arûs, 'the wedding night', for the union it was held to be, and Konya marks it every 17 December. The green-tiled dome dates from the thirteenth century and is the emblem of Konya. And the ground beneath it was once the rose garden of the Seljuk palace.
outro: This brings our tour of the Mevlâna Museum to an end. Before you go, please leave the objects untouched and take your photographs without flash. Thank you for your visit, and enjoy the rest of your day.
